g.text: the detail JSON hands back two independent readouts. one says whether the meaning survived, the other whether the position did.
readout 1 · the transport map · did each statement keep a counterpart on the other side?
one row per statement of document A
transport map · flows[3] · one statement of A and everywhere its weight landed
Cutting into statements took 2.55 s; encoding 3.0 s.
every bit of this statement's weight landed on one counterpart
how far it had to travel to get there. this trip was short
the best match was cheap enough that nothing here needs a human
all of its weight went to a single counterpart, at low cost.
transport map · flows[9] · one statement of A and everywhere its weight landed
Exact solving is faster and unbiased at this scale.
Sinkhorn wins on large point clouds.
There is no free lunch in general.
A hundred thousand pairs costs 139 core hours.
the weight split three ways. nothing over there is really this statement
and every one of those three trips was a long one
flagged. this is the row a human opens
no single counterpart on the other side. the claim was dropped, or invented.
readout 2 · the order map · a separate check, answering a separate question
and it did not move either
order map · statements[3] · the same statement as the left panel, read by the other check
how many positions it shifted between the two documents. zero means it sits exactly where it belonged
so there is nothing to fix on the ordering side
and this one did not move position either.
meaning and position are two separate readouts.
a statement can survive the rewrite and still sit in the wrong place.
